title: Two-factor authentication with an authenticator app
tasks: two-factor authentication with an authenticator app

requirements.text: Enrollment generates a CSPRNG secret (at least 160 bits) and an otpauth:// URI for the QR code
2FA becomes required only after the user submits a valid code for the new secret
Codes are verified per RFC 6238 with a small clock-skew window; malformed codes fail
An accepted time step or recovery code cannot be used again
Failed verification attempts are rate limited or locked out per account
The secret is encrypted at rest and never shown again after enrollment
One-time recovery codes are generated randomly and stored only as keyed hashes
Disabling 2FA or regenerating recovery codes requires recent re-authentication

evidence.name: secret provisioning: 160-bit CSPRNG secret in base32 and an otpauth URI with encoded issuer and label
confirm enrollment: 2FA is required only after a valid code for the pending secret
confirm enrollment: the pending secret expires and a new enrollment replaces the old pending secret
sql: schema applies; enrollment confirms only with a valid code before expiry; secret stored as ciphertext
totp matches the RFC 6238 Appendix B SHA-1 vectors (8 digits) and their 6-digit truncations
code verification: accepts the current step and one step of skew either way, rejects two steps
code verification: malformed codes fail; spaces inside a code are tolerated
replay protection: an accepted time step cannot be used again, nor an earlier step in the window
replay protection: of four concurrent verifies of one code exactly one wins (memory store)
sql: of four concurrent verifies of one code exactly one wins, and the step cannot be replayed
sql: recovery codes are single use under concurrency and regeneration replaces all of them
attempt limits: five failures per 15 minutes lock the account, even for a correct code, until the window passes
attempt limits: the recovery-code path shares the same per-account limit
attempt limits: concurrent wrong guesses cannot exceed the limit
sql: attempt limit is atomic under concurrency, shared with recovery codes, and resets after the window
secret protection: AES-256-GCM ciphertext with key id; plaintext never stored or returned after confirmation
secret protection: old keys still decrypt after rotation and reencryptSecret moves the row to the current key
recovery codes: random, stored only as HMAC-SHA-256 with the pepper, single use, case and dash insensitive
recovery codes: concurrent uses of one code, exactly one wins
step-up: disabling and regenerating require re-authentication within 10 minutes and are refused otherwise
sql: disable requires recent re-authentication and deletes the secret and codes

implementations.notes: TOTP only; render the otpauth URI with the qr-code module. Call disable and regenerateRecoveryCodes only from fully signed-in sessions (the HTTP adapter enforces the session stage).

evidence.name: totp: verify window, base32, otpauth URI and secret generation
totp: RFC 6238 Appendix B vectors
totp: verify window, base32, otpauth URI and secret generation
recovery-codes: normalize, hash, generate and find

implementations.notes: Generates, hashes and matches; removing a used code is the app's work

notes: module:two-factor covers enrollment, RFC 6238 verification, replay protection, lockout, encrypted secrets, recovery codes and step-up. The app supplies sign-in, sessions and QR rendering (qr-code module).
